entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Loads the user row, calls anonymize_user and commits; no row is deleted.

stores.name: users

fields.name: metadata_json
fields.note: A comment on the column says the value is an arbitrary key/value set by the client and that support pastes contact details into it.

erasure.note: anonymize_user writes only email and full_name, so this column keeps whatever the client and support put in it.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: Soft-delete column on the user row.

erasure.note: No code in the repository writes this column, so closing an account leaves it unset and nothing later reads it to delete the row.
close_account overwrites email with its SHA-256 hash and full_name with the constant "removed"; the row, its id and the hash of the address remain, and no delete is issued.

stores.note: Table holding the user account row.

stores.name: tickets

fields.name: notes
fields.note: A comment on the column says the free text may contain phone numbers.

erasure.note: close_account deletes no row, and the User.tickets relationship carries no cascade argument, so ticket rows and their text stay as written together with the user_id that points back to the person.

stores.note: Table holding support tickets, linked to the user by user_id.

stores.name: request_log

fields.name: ip_address
fields.note: Read from request.client.host and written to the log line at middleware.py:11.

erasure.note: The middleware writes the caller's IP address to the request_log logger on every request, and no code in the repository removes or rotates those lines.

stores.note: Python logging sink named request_log, written by the request middleware registered in app.py.
